🚨ICYMI: Last week, I introduced the bipartisan Expanding Medicare Hearing Aid Coverage Act to finally address Medicare’s outdated ban on hearing aid coverage and to provide the care our seniors deserve.

Here are the facts:

➡️ Nearly 48 million Americans suffer from hearing loss.  
➡️ The average cost of hearing aids exceeds $2,500, leaving millions unable to afford them.  
➡️ Untreated hearing loss can lead to increased risks of isolation, depression, dementia, and cognitive decline.

Great meeting today with Dr. Keith Miller, President of the Pennsylvania Chiropractic Association, a leader in his industry, as well as a proud PA-1 Chalfont resident and business owner. Our conversation focused on the vital need to move forward the Chiropractic Medicare Coverage Modernization Act.

This important bipartisan legislation, which I’ve proudly co-sponsored over the past three Congresses, will provide Medicare beneficiaries with greater access to a wider range of pain management options. It’s long past time to eliminate the outdated restrictions that prevent chiropractors from providing the full scope of care our seniors need to live healthier, more comfortable lives.

Dr. Miller and his team’s thoughtful insight and advocacy in improving access to quality care are driving real change, and I look forward to continuing working alongside them to ensure every senior has the opportunity to live a healthier, pain-free life.

At yesterday’s @WaysandMeansGOP Health Subcommittee Hearing on After the Hospital: Ensuring Access to Quality Post-Acute Care, I highlighted a critical issue facing our PA-1 community: a severe shortage of healthcare staff. This crisis is leaving our patients without care or care that falls short of their needs. Skilled Nursing Facilities (SNF) are being hit hardest, with Pennsylvania projected to face the most severe staffing shortage by 2026, and half our state’s healthcare providers planning to close or sell at least 1 of their SNF locations this year.

I turned to Dr. Dana Madison, DNP, MBA, BSN, RN of Compassion Home Health Care, to share how staffing shortages have impacted patient care. She emphasized the critical role telehealth can play in bridging this gap. Telehealth has already begun to transform healthcare, making it more accessible for patients while easing the burden on providers. We must expand, not limit, access to this vital tool.

That’s why I introduced the Telehealth Expansion Act of 2025. This bipartisan legislation will allow over 32 million Americans with High-Deductible Health Plans (HDHPs) and Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) to access telehealth services before meeting their deductible—giving families the care they need when they need it most.

Watch our exchange below: ⬇️

Every American deserves access to affordable, life-saving medications—especially those battling cancer, chronic illnesses, and autoimmune diseases.

At today’s @WaysandMeansGOP Health Subcommittee Hearing on Lowering Costs for Patients, I continued advocating for solutions that increase access and affordability—like expanding the use of biosimilars.

Biosimilars are safe, effective alternatives to costly biologics and could dramatically reduce out-of-pocket expenses. But despite their promise, outdated Medicare reimbursement policies and a lack of provider incentives have slowed their adoption.

Improving Medicare’s Part B payment model is a targeted, bipartisan solution that would help increase biosimilar use, reduce costs, and ensure more patients benefit from the full range of available therapies.

Patients shouldn’t have to choose between access and affordability. We can and must do both.

Watch my full exchange below: ⬇️

In a major victory for animals, patients, and science, the @US_FDA is finally beginning to move away from outdated animal testing.

This has been a top priority of my Congressional Animal Protection Caucus that I’ve co-chaired since joining Congress—and today, after persistent bipartisan advocacy, real change is happening.

The FDA will now allow advanced, human-based alternatives—like AI models, organoids, and global data—to replace animal testing for monoclonal antibody therapies.

This means:

✅ Fewer dogs, primates, and other animals used in testing
✅ Faster, safer treatments for patients
✅ Lower drug development costs

This is a smarter, more compassionate path forward—and one we’ve been fighting for, every step of the way.

Fixing the challenges facing our physicians and patients demands a bipartisan approach focused on real, lasting solutions.

This week, my @ProbSolveCaucus Co-Chair @RepTomSuozzi and I met with emergency physicians from @ACEPNation at #LAC25 to hear directly from those on the frontlines. Their insights on workforce shortages, overcrowding, and care delivery are helping shape the policies we’re working on in Congress right now.

This isn’t just a priority — it’s a responsibility we’re working to meet head-on. We’re taking what we heard and translating it into bipartisan solutions that meet this moment and move our healthcare system forward.

Great meeting with hospital and health system leaders from across our region—including Dr. Baligh Yehia, President of @TJUHospital—at the American Hospital Association’s Annual Meeting in Washington, D.C. Their leadership and commitment to strengthening care for patients and providers across Pennsylvania is greatly appreciated.

In Congress, I remain focused on advancing real, bipartisan solutions to strengthen our healthcare system and championing patient-centered legislation that supports our medical professionals, expands access, and lowers costs. My commitment is clear: I’ll keep fighting to protect Medicare, Medicaid, and the vital safety net programs that millions of Americans rely on for care, stability, and peace of mind.

I will always stand with our healthcare heroes—and continue working to ensure every family in our community has access to the affordable, high-quality care they deserve

Ukraine’s expertly executed strike on key Russian military airfield assets delivered a direct blow to the machinery driving Putin’s war. 

While Ukraine targets instruments of war, Putin targets innocent lives—bombing homes, hospitals, and schools. The contrast is clear and undeniable. 

The United States must respond with decisive strength. It’s time for full, unforgiving sanctions—against Putin, his regime, and every enabler of this campaign of terror—until the Russian war machine crumbles under its own weight. Peace through strength begins with action. Now.

Cybercriminals are targeting hospitals, stealing patient data, and putting lives at risk. I’ve spoken with local hospitals, health care providers, and families across our community about the real-world impacts of these breaches—and the urgent need for action.

We worked together on solutions, and this week, I introduced the bipartisan Healthcare Cybersecurity Act to strengthen our defenses and protect the systems families rely on every day.

🚨 What the bill does:

✔️ Requires CISA and HHS to coordinate real-time cyber threat response
✔️ Establishes a dedicated federal liaison to close gaps
✔️ Expands cybersecurity training for frontline health care workers
✔️ Directs a full-scale review of vulnerabilities across the health sector

Over 46 million Americans had their personal health data breached in just one year. That’s not just a privacy issue—it’s a public safety threat.

As Chairman of the CIA Subcommittee and a former FBI agent who’s worked on cybercrime firsthand, I’m leading this bipartisan effort to stay ahead of emerging threats and build a more secure, resilient future.

This is about securing patient data, strengthening our hospitals’ defenses, and giving health care providers the tools they need to stay ahead of growing threats.

🔗: https://t.co/SkTR2qGSQk

Cancer remains one of the deadliest diseases in America—and now, patients are facing another threat: drug shortages that delay or deny lifesaving treatment.

That’s why I introduced the Knock Out Cancer Act—bipartisan legislation that takes decisive, targeted action:

✅ 25% annual increase in funding for the National Cancer Institute over 5 years
✅ Requires HHS to investigate cancer drug shortages and deliver concrete solutions to Congress within 1 year 

As Co-Chair of the House Cancer Caucus, I’m working to push for stronger research, faster innovation, and better access to care. This bill is one of the most serious efforts in years to meet the scale of the crisis, and I’m committed to getting it across the finish line.

🔗: https://t.co/vJh8iPZY71

Cyberattacks are hitting our hospitals harder than ever—putting lives at risk, exposing patient data, and straining care delivery.

After meeting with healthcare leaders across our community who raised the alarm, I introduced the bipartisan Healthcare Cybersecurity Act in direct partnership with providers on the frontlines.

The bill strengthens coordination between CISA and HHS, expands cybersecurity training, and equips hospitals with the tools to detect and stop threats in real time.

This is about protecting patients, defending care, and ensuring our healthcare system is ready for the threats of today—and tomorrow.

Access to quality dermatological care saves lives — and it starts with fair reimbursement and preventive screenings.

That’s why I sat down with the American Academy of Dermatology and PA-1’s own Roman Bronfenbrener of Warminster to advance solutions that protect patients and providers alike.

As a cosponsor of H.R. 879, I’m leading efforts to reverse the looming 2025 Medicare cut and secure an inflationary adjustment—critical steps to keep care accessible and sustainable. We also zeroed in on the life-saving power of preventive screenings and early detection, an issue I’ve long championed to improve access to care and public health. 

Thank you to the @AADskin and Roman for your partnership and showing how local voices can shape national policy. I look forward to continuing to work together to ensure every patient has access to the care they need and deliver real solutions for PA-1 and beyond.

When public policy and private innovation come together, patients win, and our PA-1 community leads the way.

I sat down with Bristol Myers Squibb’s local leaders, Michelle Hudson of Newtown (VP Drug Development Portfolio), Brian Turner of Langhorne (VP Corporate Security), and Dana Walker of Chalfont (VP Global Program Lead), to advance policies that drive pharmaceutical innovation, expand research in neurology and mental health, and combat the surge of counterfeit and stolen drugs worldwide.

We focused on correcting current harmful legal provisions and mapped out next steps to protect patients, safeguard the global drug supply chain, and accelerate new treatments and cures.

Thank you to @bmsnews and Michelle, Brian, and Dana for your leadership and continued collaboration— together we’re keeping our community at the forefront of lifesaving innovation.

Today at the Ways and Means Committee markup, I spoke in strong support of H.R. 842, the Nancy Gardner Sewell Medicare Multi-Cancer Early Detection Screening Coverage Act—introduced by my friend, @RepTerriSewell, and which I’m proud to co-sponsor.

This bipartisan bill ensures that Medicare covers FDA-approved multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests without delay, giving seniors timely access to cutting-edge screening that can detect dozens of cancers—often before symptoms appear.

As Co-Chair of the Congressional Cancer Caucus, this fight is personal. I’ve made it my mission to advance earlier detection, faster access, and smarter cancer policy. We have the science. We have the technology. What we need now is urgency.

We cannot let red tape stand in the way of a second chance.

H.R. 842 is how we change the story.

Let’s pass this bill. And let’s make early detection the standard—not the exception.

There is no America without BAC craftworkers.

For over a century, the skilled hands of our bricklayers, stone masons, tile setters, cement masons, plasterers, and restoration specialists have built the schools where we learn, the hospitals where we heal, and the public buildings that anchor our communities—literally laying the foundation of our nation.

This morning, I was honored to join my friends at the BAC National Convention to listen, learn, and say thank you. Together, we will continue to protect the right to organize through my PRO Act, defend strong labor standards, and keep union jobs flowing through the Infrastructure Investment & Jobs Act, which I was proud to help drive across the finish line. And together we will march forward—to expand opportunity, strengthen protections, and deliver even more wins for the trades.

Thank you to my friend and National President Tim Driscoll, to our PA-1 BAC members for joining me, and to every BAC craftworker across our nation for your leadership, your service, and your enduring role in building America’s future.

Today, I visited two of our region’s most vital pediatric institutions, Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia and St. Christopher’s Hospital for Children, for a critical conversation on the future of children’s health care and the mounting challenges facing pediatric hospitals nationwide.

For decades, @ChildrensPhila and St. Chris have delivered world-class, compassionate care to hundreds of thousands of children and families in our community and across the Commonwealth, regardless of background, income, or diagnosis. From breakthroughs in rare disease treatment to everyday care that keeps kids healthy, their work doesn’t just heal—it saves lives. 

Yet the critical care they provide is increasingly under strain. The widening gap between rising costs and Medicaid shortfalls is pushing even our strongest safety-net hospitals to a breaking point.

I’ve always fought to protect and strengthen Medicaid and CHIP, and I’ll continue working closely with the exceptional leadership teams at CHOP and St. Chris to ensure they have the resources, support, and long-term stability they need. That includes championing the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act of 2025, which I am proud to co-sponsor, advancing a special Medicaid designation for children’s hospitals, and securing greater NIH investment in pediatric research. Our children’s health is non-negotiable, and I’ll keep working to ensure these institutions can continue their lifesaving mission without compromise. @hospitals4kids

Modernizing care coordination for Medicare patients has been one of my top health care priorities—and yesterday’s Ways & Means Health Subcommittee hearing underscored exactly why this work must continue.

Chronic disease now defines the Medicare population. Yet instead of coordinated care, seniors are facing:

✔️50% more specialist visits than two years ago
✔️ Thousands in preventable costs per patient
✔️ Physicians stretched too thin to focus on quality care

I focused my questioning to Dr. Michael Hoben and Dr. Ashish Parikh on two reforms I’ve been driving:

1️⃣ Making telehealth a permanent pillar of chronic care
2️⃣ Modernizing Medicare’s physician payment system

Their message was clear:

✔ Telehealth is a core tool for stabilizing chronic disease, avoiding emergencies, and lowering costs
✔ Value-based models measurably improve outcomes—from higher screening rates to fewer hospitalizations—while saving Medicare money

When telehealth payments briefly lapsed during the shutdown, we saw how quickly access can be disrupted. Permanent telehealth reliability and a modern payment system must remain central to this work, and I will continue driving it forward.

We’ve been navigating a difficult landscape with one priority: protecting families from premium spikes and preserving affordable coverage.

The plan we’ve built reflects that work—a responsible, two-party approach rooted in common sense, free of partisan riders, and built to earn the support needed to become law and deliver real relief.

I joined CNN’s @mkraju to discuss the status of our bipartisan legislation to address the rising costs of healthcare.  Our bipartisan plan protects families from higher costs and keeps the coverage they rely on affordable. It’s been built the right way—across the aisle and across chambers—with a pathway to 218 and 60 in mind.

Families need a fix, and that’s what we’re bringing to the floor.
